title: Contact and Non-contact Forces
seo_title: Primary 3 Basic Science: Contact and Non-contact Forces Worksheets (NERDC)
standard_code: Primary 3 Basic Science: You and Energy
standard_text: Forces are pushes or pulls; contact forces (friction, applied force) act when objects touch, and non-contact forces (gravity, magnetic and electric forces) act at a distance. Forces change the motion and shape of objects. (summary of the Basic Science curriculum, Primary 3, theme: You and Energy)
meta_desc: Free Primary 3 Basic Science worksheets (NERDC curriculum, theme: You and Energy): contact and non-contact forces, effects of forces, balanced and unbalanced forces, magnets and gravity. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Contact forces need touching; non-contact forces act at a distance.
body_html:
How to think about it

A force is a push or a pull. Contact forces act when objects touch, such as kicking a ball or friction. Non-contact forces act at a distance: gravity pulls things down, magnets attract iron, and static electricity attracts small bits of paper.

Forces can make objects start, stop, speed up, slow down, change direction or change shape. When forces on an object are balanced, its motion does not change; unbalanced forces change its motion.

Example

Is gravity a contact force?

Does it need touching?

Answer: no, it is a non-contact force

Example

Two teams pull a rope with equal force. What happens?

Balanced

Answer: the rope does not move

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a force is needed to keep an object moving at the same speed.
  • Thinking magnets must touch to attract.
  • Thinking balanced forces mean no forces.
